survey.title: A Survey of Large Language Models
survey.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have drawn a lot of attention due to their strong performance on a wide range of natural language processing tasks. This survey provides a comprehensive review of the recent advances in LLMs.

gpt3.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
gpt3.highlight: GPT-3 with 175B parameters demonstrated strong few-shot learning capabilities without gradient updates, sparking the era of large language models.
gpt3.contribution: Scaled autoregressive language models to 175B parameters. Demonstrated emergent few-shot learning where the model performs tasks given only natural language prompts and examples. Showed that model performance scales smoothly with model size, dataset size, and compute.

ablationStudy.finding: Few-shot performance improves smoothly and predictably with model scale
Performance increases with number of in-context examples up to model context limit
Model highly sensitive to prompt formatting and example ordering

llama.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
llama.highlight: Open foundation models (7B-65B) trained on publicly available data only, showing that smaller models trained longer can match larger proprietary models.
llama.contribution: Released open weights for 7B, 13B, 33B, and 65B parameter models. Trained only on publicly available datasets. Demonstrated that smaller models trained on more tokens outperform larger models trained on fewer tokens (Chinchilla scaling laws).

ablationStudy.finding: Training longer on more data more important than scaling parameters (Chinchilla)
SwiGLU activation improves perplexity over ReLU
Pre-normalization with RMSNorm stabilizes training at scale

llama2.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
llama2.highlight: Improved open LLMs (7B-70B) with 40% more training data, longer context, and Grouped-Query Attention for inference efficiency.
llama2.contribution: Released base and chat-tuned models up to 70B. Introduced Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) for faster inference. Trained on 2T tokens with better data cleaning. Released extensive safety evaluations and red-teaming reports.
datasets: New publicly available online data sources

ablationStudy.finding: GQA maintains quality while reducing KV-cache memory by ~30%
Technique to maintain multi-turn instruction adherence
Safety fine-tuning slightly hurts helpfulness scores but dramatically reduces harmful outputs

t5.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
t5.highlight: T5 reframes all NLP tasks as text-to-text problems and systematically studies the effects of architecture, pre-training objectives, and datasets.
t5.contribution: Proposed a unified text-to-text framework where every task is cast as text generation. Introduced the C4 dataset. Conducted extensive ablations on architecture, unsupervised objectives, and fine-tuning approaches.

ablationStudy.finding: Span corruption (replace random spans with single mask token) outperforms BERT-style MLM
Encoder-decoder superior for fine-tuning; decoder-only competitive for generation
Performance improves log-linearly with pre-training dataset size

switch-transformer.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
switch-transformer.highlight: Switch Transformer scales to 1.6T parameters using sparse Mixture-of-Experts with each token routing to only 1 expert, achieving 7x pre-training speedup.
switch-transformer.contribution: Simplified MoE by routing each token to a single expert (top-1 routing). Scaled to 1.6T parameters with same computational cost as a 10B dense model. Demonstrated positive transfer across multilingual tasks.

ablationStudy.finding: Top-1 routing sufficient; top-2 adds complexity without clear benefit
Capacity factor 1.0 balances quality and training stability
Essential for preventing expert collapse; too high hurts quality

mixtral.title: Mixtral of Experts
mixtral.highlight: Mixtral 8x7B: A sparse MoE model that outperforms Llama 2 70B while being 6x faster at inference, using only 2 active experts per token.
mixtral.contribution: Released open-weight sparse MoE with 8 experts (46.7B total, 12.9B active). Each layer routes to top-2 experts. Outperformed Llama 2 70B on most benchmarks while using fewer active parameters.

ablationStudy.finding: Top-2 experts provides best quality/latency tradeoff
Allows 32K context with linear attention complexity beyond window

instructgpt.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
instructgpt.highlight: InstructGPT: Fine-tuned GPT-3 with supervised fine-tuning and RLHF to better follow instructions, preferred by human evaluators over 100x larger GPT-3.
instructgpt.contribution: Proposed the RLHF pipeline: SFT on human demonstrations, then train reward model from human preferences, then optimize policy with PPO against the reward model. 1.3B InstructGPT preferred over 175B GPT-3. Introduced the important insight that alignment can trade off some capabilities for better usefulness.

trainingSetting.stage2: Reward model trained on ~33K comparison labels
trainingSetting.stage3: PPO optimization with KL divergence constraint

ablationStudy.finding: KL coefficient 0.02 prevents reward hacking while maintaining gains
6B reward model sufficient; scaling beyond doesn't help much
RLHF significantly outperforms SFT-only in human preference

dpo.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
dpo.highlight: DPO eliminates the need for explicit reward modeling and PPO, directly optimizing the LLM on preference data with a simple classification loss.
dpo.contribution: Derived that the Bradley-Terry reward model can be reparameterized in terms of the optimal policy, eliminating separate reward model training. Proposed Direct Preference Optimization as a simple alternative to RLHF/PPO. Showed comparable or better performance with simpler implementation.

ablationStudy.finding: Beta controls KL divergence; 0.1 works well across tasks
Using frozen SFT model as reference prevents mode collapse
Implicit DPO reward correlates well with explicit reward model

flan.title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
flan.highlight: FLAN: Fine-tuning a language model on a collection of datasets phrased as instructions substantially improves zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks.
flan.contribution: Introduced instruction tuning: fine-tuning on diverse NLP tasks expressed via natural language instructions. Compiled FLAN dataset with 62 NLP datasets. Demonstrated strong zero-shot generalization to held-out task types.
datasets: 62 NLP datasets grouped into 12 task clusters

ablationStudy.finding: More diverse task clusters improve generalization; diminishing returns after ~10 clusters
Adding chain-of-thought examples to instructions improves reasoning
Instruction tuning benefits increase with model size (emergent at 8B+)

cot.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
cot.highlight: Chain-of-Thought prompting: simply adding 'Let's think step by step' examples dramatically improves LLM performance on complex reasoning tasks.
cot.contribution: Proposed chain-of-thought prompting: providing step-by-step reasoning examples in the prompt. Showed large emergent gains on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks. Demonstrated that CoT benefits scale strongly with model size.

ablationStudy.finding: CoT only helps at scale (>100B parameters); hurts smaller models
Correct reasoning chains essential; incorrect examples propagate errors
Explicit 'Let's think step by step' phrase critical for zero-shot CoT

toolformer.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
toolformer.highlight: Toolformer teaches LLMs to decide when and how to call external APIs (calculator, search, translator, calendar) via self-supervised learning.
toolformer.contribution: Proposed a self-supervised method to teach LLMs API usage. The model generates API calls, executes them, and keeps only calls that reduce perplexity. Demonstrated tool use for calculator, QA system, search engine, translator, and calendar.

ablationStudy.finding: Perplexity reduction most effective filter; random sampling hurts performance
Training with multiple APIs simultaneously improves each individual API use
Sampling API calls proportional to predicted usefulness improves precision
